## Critical-Severity OpenSSL Vulnerabilities Published in 2022

Only **one** true OpenSSL critical CVE was published by NVD in 2022:

---

### 🔴 CVE-2022-2274 — OpenSSL 3.0.4 RSA Remote Code Execution
| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Published** | July 1, 2022 |
| **CVSS v3.1 Score** | **9.8 / 10 (CRITICAL)** |
| **Vector** | Network / No auth required / No user interaction |
| **CWE** | CWE-787 (Out-of-Bounds Write / Memory Corruption) |
| **Affected Version** | OpenSSL **3.0.4 only** |

**Description:**
OpenSSL 3.0.4 introduced a serious bug in its **RSA implementation** for x86-64 CPUs that support **AVX512IFMA instructions**. When using 2048-bit RSA private keys on such hardware, a memory corruption bug is triggered during cryptographic computation. This corruption can allow a remote attacker to achieve **remote code execution (RCE)** on the affected machine.

**Who is affected?**
- SSL/TLS servers (or any server using 2048-bit RSA private keys) running **OpenSSL 3.0.4** on x86-64 machines with AVX512IFMA CPU support.

**Fix:**
Upgrade to OpenSSL 3.0.5 or later (patch commit referenced in the [official advisory](https://www.openssl.org/news/secadv/20220705.txt)).

---

**Notable context:** The much-hyped **CVE-2022-3786 and CVE-2022-3602** (the "spooky" OpenSSL 3.x buffer overflows disclosed in November 2022) were initially feared to be Critical but were **downgraded to HIGH severity** before public release, so they do not appear here. CVE-2022-2274 stands as the sole Critical-rated OpenSSL vulnerability of 2022 per NVD.
